title: Preference optimisation (DPO) and AI-judge labels
paper: Rafailov et al. 2023, Direct Preference Optimization; Bai et al. 2022 (RLAIF)
claim: DPO on preference pairs raises the model's preference for the chosen response without a separate reward model, and AI-judge labels can replace human labels.
setup: EleutherAI/pythia-70m fine-tuned with trl DPOTrainer (beta=0.1, lr=1e-05, 1 epoch) on 400 short Anthropic HH helpful-base pairs, evaluated on 200 held-out pairs, 3 seeds. AI labels come from Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (local, both answer orders scored). watsonx.ai Granite judge: not run (no key).
result: Held-out pairs where the model ranks the human-chosen reply higher (length-normalised log-likelihood): untrained 49.0%, DPO on human labels 54.7 ± 0.8%, DPO on judge labels 56.2 ± 1.8%. DPO implicit-reward accuracy: human 59.2 ± 2.5%, judge 55.8 ± 3.8%. Rule-based quality pass rate: untrained 10%, human 15%, judge 12%. The judge agrees with human labels on 58.3% of 600 pairs (chance = 50%); the agreement figure uses the order-debiased score (A-B logit gap averaged over both answer orders); the judge picked the same underlying reply in both orders for only 0% of pairs (0 of 600), i.e. it is dominated by position bias.
verdict_reason: Capped at 'partly': the held-out set is small (binomial SE about 3.5 points) and the judge-label arm is not better than human labels. DPO on human labels moves held-out preference accuracy by +5.7 points vs the untrained model (seed std 0.8). This is tiny scale: 70M parameters, 400 pairs.
mismatches: pythia-70m is a base model, not instruction-tuned, so 'better responses' cannot be judged by humans or meaningfully by a rule; the rule check only catches degenerate or role-leaking output.
The 0.5B local judge is weak; its agreement with humans should be read against the 50% chance level.
Preference accuracy on held-out pairs is a proxy; we did not run a win-rate evaluation.
The untrained model's implicit-reward accuracy is 0 by construction (policy equals reference).
IBM watsonx.ai Granite judge adapter exists in prayog/judge.py but was not run.
